newsitem.title: LEBANON: Israeli planes hit Hizbollah in south Lebanon.
newsitem.headline: Israeli planes hit Hizbollah in south Lebanon.

text.p: Israeli planes raided suspected guerrilla targets in south Lebanon on Tuesday night shortly after a guerrilla attack on two Israeli army posts, guerrilla and pro-Israeli militia sources said.

A Hizbollah spokesman in Beirut told Reuters the air attack targeted Jabal Sojoud area in Iqlim al-Toufah ridge used by the pro-Iranian guerrillas to wage attacks on Israeli forces occupying a border zone to the south.
There was no immediate word on casualties in the air raid.
"Two Israeli warplanes fired two air-to-surface missiles into Jabal Sojoud at 6.45 p.m. (1645 GMT)," the Hizbollah (Party of God) spokesman said.

Sources with the Israeli-backed South Lebanon Army (SLA) militia said the Israeli jets raided Iqlim al-Toufah after guerrillas attacked two Israeli posts on the edge of the Israeli-held zone. No one was hurt in the assaults, they said.
Hizbollah, which leads a guerrilla war in a bid to oust Israeli and SLA forces from the 15-km (nine-mile) deep buffer strip in south Lebanon, claimed responsibility for the attacks.
The group said in a statement issued in Beirut that one group of its fighters attacked the Sojoud post manned by Israeli forces at about 5 p.m. using machinegun and rocket fire, scoring direct hits.
A second group of guerrillas concurrently fired shells at the Sojoud post and the nearby Beir Kallab post, the statement added.
Some 1,000 Israeli troops and the 3,000-strong SLA hold the south Lebanon zone set up by Israel in 1985 to protect its northern border area from guerrilla raids.
